For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	# sequence-engine
2	
3	Small sequence model engine with explicit truncated backpropagation, written so that truncation points and hidden-state resets are observable from the public API.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	    python3 -m pip install -e .
12	
13	## Run
14	
15	    python3 -m sequence_engine --selftest
16	
17	The built-in self-check runs only in memory (including the incremental
18	checkpoint path) and writes no files.
19	
20	## Public interface
21	
22	`sequence_engine.Tensor(data)` and `sequence_engine.Sequential(modules)`.
23	- `Tensor.tolist() -> list`, `Tensor.shape -> list[int]`.
24	- `Sequential.forward(batch, hidden=None) -> (output, hidden)`.
25	- `Sequential.backward(loss) -> None` accumulates gradients.
26	  `loss` is a scalar/Tensor seed or the tuple form `(output, upstream)`
27	  carrying the exact Tensor returned by the preceding `forward`.
28	  Calling `backward` without a preceding `forward`, or twice for one
29	  `forward`, raises `RuntimeError`. If a layer raises mid-pass the partial
30	  gradients are rolled back and the same `backward` may be retried; a retry
31	  is not a second backward.
32	- `Sequential.zero_grad() -> None` clears accumulated gradients.
33	- `Sequential.update(learning_rate) -> None` performs one in-place step
34	  `theta <- theta - learning_rate * grad` on every parameter. Gradients are
35	  not cleared; parameters without a gradient are unchanged. A non-finite or
36	  non-numeric learning rate raises `ValueError`.
37	- `Sequential.parameters() -> list[Tensor]` in registration order.
38	- `Sequential.save(target) -> None` fixes parameters, accumulated gradients
39	  (zeros for parameters that have none), the slice-boundary hidden state and
40	  the layer order in one versioned binary checkpoint. `target` is a
41	  filesystem path (`str`/`os.PathLike`), an existing directory used as an
42	  incremental checkpoint chain, a `MemoryChain`, or an in-memory
43	  `bytearray`; saving mutates no existing state and repeated saves of the
44	  same state produce identical bytes. A boundary exists before the first
45	  segment and after every `forward` -- the hidden state returned by that
46	  forward *is* the boundary -- so saving is allowed even when the latest
47	  forward has not been back-propagated yet; the snapshot fixes the boundary
48	  state, not the in-flight activations.
49	- `Sequential.load(source) -> hidden | None` restores a checkpoint from a
50	  path, an incremental-chain directory, a `MemoryChain`, or bytes-like
51	  buffer and returns the restored hidden-state list for the next
52	  `forward(batch, hidden)`. The format version (the previous format version
53	  1 is read and migrated item by item; `Sequential.loaded_from_version`
54	  reports the version a successful load came from), every tensor shape and
55	  the layer order (count, layer kinds, per-layer parameter shapes) are
56	  checked first; hidden-state shapes are verified on the spot, even for a
57	  model that has never run a forward. Any mismatch, truncation, corruption
58	  or missing field rejects the whole checkpoint with `ValueError` -- nothing
59	  is partially applied or silently filled in. A missing path raises
60	  `FileNotFoundError`.
61	
62	### Threading
63	
64	All `Sequential` operations are serialised by one per-container lock, so
65	multiple threads may interleave `forward`, `backward`, `update`, `save` and
66	`load`. Under any interleaving each parameter's final value is one a serial
67	execution of the same calls could have produced: `update` applies as one
68	atomic step, a `load` is never observed half-applied, and no `save` can read
69	a half-written tensor. Every snapshot corresponds to one complete slice
70	boundary -- never two passes half mixed. When two threads save to the same
71	file path the bytes on disk are always one or the other writer's complete
72	checkpoint (never a blend).
73	
74	## Checkpoint file semantics
75	
76	Path saves are atomic: bytes go to a temporary file in the destination
77	directory, which is `os.replace`d over any existing file (no backup is
78	kept). A process killed mid-write leaves only the rejected temporary file;
79	the final path either holds the previous complete checkpoint or the new
80	one. A half-written or corrupted file at the load path is detected by its
81	trailer and CRC and refused with `ValueError`.
82	
83	Floats are stored as raw IEEE-754 float64 values, so a save/load round-trip
84	is bitwise identical, including the sign of negative zero. Integers must
85	fit in int64 and all serialized numbers must be finite; oversized integers
86	or non-finite floats raise `ValueError` on save, and a payload that merely
87	contains an oversized or non-finite value is refused on load. Saving into
88	a directory that does not exist or is not writable, or failing because the
89	disk is full, raises `OSError`; the caller chooses the destination path.
90	
91	## Checkpoint format versions
92	
93	The on-disk format is versioned. This build writes **version 2** and still
94	reads **version 1**: an old file is migrated item by item into the current
95	document shape and the source version is recorded; if migration fails on
96	any item the whole file is rejected rather than silently filled in. A file
97	with an unknown version, or a header with a field added or removed, is
98	rejected with `ValueError`. A migrated state re-saves as native version 2.
99	Unknown (future) versions are never guessed; they are refused.
100	
101	## Incremental checkpoint chains
102	
103	Passing an existing directory (or a `MemoryChain`) to `save`/`load` uses an
104	incremental chain instead of one self-contained file:
105	
106	- the first save writes a full **basis** segment (`seg-0000000000.seqd`);
107	- every later save appends a delta segment naming only the tensors that
108	  changed, compared by encoded leaf identity (so float sign bits such as
109	  `-0.0` count); unchanged saves append an empty delta deterministically,
110	  and layers with no parameters participate like any other layer;
111	- a `head` pointer names the newest committed segment. Each segment file is
112	  written completely and atomically before the head is advanced, so a crash,
113	  a full disk or two saves racing into one directory always leave a single
114	  complete chain reachable from `head`.
115	
116	Loading walks the basis and every delta up to the head and reassembles the
117	state by layer. The reassembled state is bit for bit identical to the full
118	snapshot taken at the same moment. Any segment in the chain that is
119	truncated, corrupt, missing a field, out of order, changes the layer order
120	or parameter/shapes, or introduces hidden state incompletely makes the load
121	reject the **whole** chain with `ValueError`. A missing chain directory or a
122	referenced segment file that is absent raises `FileNotFoundError`; an
123	unwritable directory or a full disk raises `OSError`. A chain cannot change
124	the model's layer order or parameter shapes -- use a fresh full snapshot for
125	a different model.
126	
127	`MemoryChain` (exported from `sequence_engine`) is an in-memory chain with
128	identical commit semantics, useful for tests and long-running processes that
129	want incremental snapshots without files.
130	
131	## Tests
132	
133	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
134	
135	## Limits
136	
137	CPU only; no GPU backend.
138	One backward pass per forward pass.
139	The engine trains nothing on its own and ships no dataset.
140

    python3 -m sequence_engine --selftest

All `Sequential` operations are serialised by one per-container lock, so

`load`. Under any interleaving each parameter's final value is one a serial
execution of the same calls could have produced: `update` applies as one
atomic step, a `load` is never observed half-applied, and no `save` can read
a half-written tensor. Every snapshot corresponds to one complete slice
boundary -- never two passes half mixed. When two threads save to the same
file path the bytes on disk are always one or the other writer's complete
checkpoint (never a blend).

## Checkpoint file semantics

Path saves are atomic: bytes go to a temporary file in the destination
directory, which is `os.replace`d over any existing file (no backup is
kept). A process killed mid-write leaves only the rejected temporary file;
the final path either holds the previous complete checkpoint or the new
one. A half-written or corrupted file at the load path is detected by its
trailer and CRC and refused with `ValueError`.

Floats are stored as raw IEEE-754 float64 values, so a save/load round-trip
is bitwise identical, including the sign of negative zero. Integers must
fit in int64 and all serialized numbers must be finite; oversized integers
or non-finite floats raise `ValueError` on save, and a payload that merely
contains an oversized or non-finite value is refused on load. Saving into
a directory that does not exist or is not writable, or failing because the
disk is full, raises `OSError`; the caller chooses the destination path.

## Checkpoint format versions

The on-disk format is versioned. This build writes **version 2** and still
reads **version 1**: an old file is migrated item by item into the current
document shape and the source version is recorded; if migration fails on
any item the whole file is rejected rather than silently filled in. A file
with an unknown version, or a header with a field added or removed, is
rejected with `ValueError`. A migrated state re-saves as native version 2.
Unknown (future) versions are never guessed; they are refused.

## Incremental checkpoint chains

Passing an existing directory (or a `MemoryChain`) to `save`/`load` uses an
incremental chain instead of one self-contained file:

- the first save writes a full **basis** segment (`seg-0000000000.seqd`);
- every later save appends a delta segment naming only the tensors that
  changed, compared by encoded leaf identity (so float sign bits such as
  `-0.0` count); unchanged saves append an empty delta deterministically,
  and layers with no parameters participate like any other layer;
- a `head` pointer names the newest committed segment. Each segment file is
  written completely and atomically before the head is advanced, so a crash,
  a full disk or two saves racing into one directory always leave a single
  complete chain reachable from `head`.

Loading walks the basis and every delta up to the head and reassembles the
state by layer. The reassembled state is bit for bit identical to the full
snapshot taken at the same moment. Any segment in the chain that is
truncated, corrupt, missing a field, out of order, changes the layer order
or parameter/shapes, or introduces hidden state incompletely makes the load
reject the **whole** chain with `ValueError`. A missing chain directory or a
referenced segment file that is absent raises `FileNotFoundError`; an
unwritable directory or a full disk raises `OSError`. A chain cannot change
the model's layer order or parameter shapes -- use a fresh full snapshot for
a different model.

`MemoryChain` (exported from `sequence_engine`) is an in-memory chain with
identical commit semantics, useful for tests and long-running processes that
want incremental snapshots without files.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

## Limits

CPU only; no GPU backend.
One backward pass per forward pass.
The engine trains nothing on its own and ships no dataset.

8	def _normalize(data):
9	    """Validate *data* and return ``(shape, deep-copied nested lists)``."""
10	    if isinstance(data, bool):
11	        raise ValueError("Tensor data must be numeric; booleans are not allowed")
12	    if isinstance(data, (int, float)):
13	        return [], data
14	    if isinstance(data, (list, tuple)):
15	        if len(data) == 0:
16	            raise ValueError("Tensor data must not be empty")
17	        shape = None
18	        items = []
19	        for item in data:
20	            sub_shape, value = _normalize(item)
21	            if shape is None:
22	                shape = sub_shape
23	            elif sub_shape != shape:
24	                raise ValueError(
25	                    "Tensor data is ragged: nested sequences must all have the same shape"
26	                )
27	            items.append(value)
28	        return [len(items)] + shape, items
29	    raise ValueError(
30	        "Tensor data must be a number or a nested sequence of numbers, "
31	        f"got {type(data).__name__}"
32	    )
33	
34	
35	def _deep_copy(value):
36	    if isinstance(value, list):
37	        return [_deep_copy(item) for item in value]
38	    return value

41	class Tensor:
42	    """An n-dimensional container of numbers with a ``grad`` slot.
43	
44	    ``grad`` starts as ``None``; layers accumulate gradients onto it and
45	    ``Sequential.zero_grad()`` resets it to an all-zeros tensor.
46	    """
47	
48	    __slots__ = ("_data", "_shape", "grad")
49	
50	    def __init__(self, data):
51	        self._shape, self._data = _normalize(data)
52	        self.grad = None
53	
54	    @property
55	    def shape(self):
56	        return list(self._shape)
57	
58	    def tolist(self):
59	        return _deep_copy(self._data)
60	
61	    def __repr__(self):
62	        return f"Tensor(shape={self._shape}, data={self._data!r})"
63	
64	    # -- internal engine hooks (not part of the public README surface) ------
65	
66	    def _values(self):
67	        """Return the raw nested storage (not a copy)."""
68	        return self._data
69	
70	    def _set_values(self, values):
71	        """Replace the raw nested storage with an already-validated tree."""
72	        self._data = values
73	
74	    def _scaled_subtract_(self, other, scale):
75	        """Subtract *scale* times *other* in place, element by element.
76	
77	        The arithmetic happens in a fixed left-to-right order so the
78	        result is identical to an uninterrupted run.
79	        """
80	        self._data = _scaled_subtract(self._data, other._data, float(scale))
81	
82	    def _all_finite(self):
83	        return _all_finite(self._data)
84	
85	
86	def _scaled_subtract(a, b, scale):
87	    if isinstance(a, list):
88	        return [_scaled_subtract(x, y, scale) for x, y in zip(a, b)]
89	    return a - scale * b
90	
91	
92	def _all_finite(value):
93	    if isinstance(value, list):
94	        return all(_all_finite(item) for item in value)
95	    return isinstance(value, int) or (
96	        isinstance(value, float) and math.isfinite(value)
97	    )

3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import threading
6	
7	from . import checkpoint as _checkpoint
8	from .tensor import Tensor
9	
10	_REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES = ("forward", "backward", "parameters")
11	
12	
13	def _zeros(shape):
14	    if not shape:
15	        return 0.0
16	    return [_zeros(shape[1:]) for _ in range(shape[0])]
17	
18	
19	def _layer_kind(module):
20	    kind = getattr(module, "checkpoint_kind", None)
21	    if kind is None:
22	        kind = type(module).__name__
23	    if not isinstance(kind, str) or not kind:
24	        raise ValueError("layer checkpoint_kind must be a non-empty string")

28	class Sequential:
29	    """Chains caller-provided layers in registration order.
30	
31	    Each layer must provide ``forward``, ``backward`` and ``parameters``.
32	    ``forward(batch, hidden=None)`` runs the batch through every layer in
33	    order; each layer consumes the previous layer's output plus its own
34	    hidden-state slot (``None`` when no hidden state is supplied, meaning
35	    the layer restarts from zeros) and returns an ``(output, hidden_slot)``
36	    pair. The slots stack in registration order into the chain's hidden
37	    state.
38	
39	    The engine keeps no gradient history across ``forward`` calls: hidden
40	    states carry values only, so a backward pass on a later segment can
41	    never add gradients to an earlier one. ``backward(loss)`` starts from
42	    the caller-computed scalar loss and walks the layers in reverse order,
43	    each layer passing the upstream gradient back and accumulating
44	    parameter gradients on its own tensors.
45	
46	    Besides the forward/backward cycle the container offers:
47	
48	    * ``update(learning_rate)`` -- one in-place gradient step
49	      ``theta <- theta - lr * grad`` on every parameter; gradients are
50	      not cleared (``zero_grad`` still does that).
51	    * ``save(target)`` / ``load(source)`` -- atomic, versioned snapshots of
52	      parameters, accumulated gradients and slice-boundary hidden state,
53	      to a filesystem path, an incremental-chain directory or to an
54	      in-memory ``bytearray``.
55	
56	    All public operations are serialised by one re-entrant lock, so
57	    several threads may interleave ``forward``, ``backward``, ``update``,
58	    ``save`` and ``load`` calls: every observed parameter state is one a
59	    serial execution of the same calls could have produced, ``update`` is
60	    atomic and a snapshot always corresponds to one complete slice
61	    boundary -- never two passes half mixed.
62	    """
63	
64	    def __init__(self, modules):
65	        if isinstance(modules, (str, bytes)):
66	            raise ValueError("Sequential expects a non-empty sequence of layers")
67	        try:
68	            modules = list(modules)
69	        except TypeError:
70	            raise ValueError(
71	                "Sequential expects a non-empty sequence of layers"
72	            ) from None
73	        if len(modules) == 0:
74	            raise ValueError("Sequential requires at least one layer")
75	        for index, module in enumerate(modules):
76	            missing = [
77	                name
78	                for name in _REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES
79	                if not callable(getattr(module, name, None))
80	            ]
81	            if missing:
82	                raise ValueError(
83	                    f"layer at index {index} is missing required "
84	                    f"capabilit{'ies' if len(missing) > 1 else 'y'}: "
85	                    + ", ".join(missing)
86	                )
87	        self._modules = modules
88	        self._pending_backward = False
89	        self._hidden_shapes = None
90	        self._last_output = None
91	        self._last_hidden = None
92	        # Version a checkpoint was loaded from (None until the first load).
93	        self._loaded_from_version = None
94	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
95	
96	    @property
97	    def loaded_from_version(self):
98	        """Format version the last ``load`` migrated from (``None`` before).
99	
100	        A version-1 checkpoint reports ``1``; a native version-2 file
101	        reports ``2``. The source version is only updated on a successful
102	        load -- a checkpoint rejected mid-migration leaves the previous
103	        value untouched.
104	        """
105	        return self._loaded_from_version
106	
107	    def forward(self, batch, hidden=None):
108	        with self._lock:
109	            if not isinstance(batch, Tensor):
110	                raise ValueError("batch must be a Tensor")
111	            batch_shape = batch.shape
112	            if len(batch_shape) == 0 or batch_shape[0] <= 0:
113	                raise ValueError("batch must be non-empty")
114	            slots = self._prepare_hidden(hidden)
115	            x = batch
116	            new_hidden = []
117	            for module, slot in zip(self._modules, slots):
118	                result = module.forward(x, slot)
119	                try:
120	                    x, slot_out = result
121	                except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
122	                    raise ValueError(
123	                        "each layer's forward must return an (output, hidden) pair"
124	                    ) from exc
125	                if not isinstance(x, Tensor) or not isinstance(slot_out, Tensor):
126	                    raise ValueError(
127	                        "each layer's forward must return (Tensor, Tensor)"
128	                    )
129	                new_hidden.append(slot_out)
130	            self._hidden_shapes = [slot.shape for slot in new_hidden]
131	            self._last_output = x
132	            self._last_hidden = new_hidden
133	            self._pending_backward = True
134	            return x, new_hidden
135	
136	    def backward(self, loss):
137	        with self._lock:
138	            if not self._pending_backward:
139	                raise RuntimeError(
140	                    "backward() requires a preceding forward() and may only be "
141	                    "called once per forward()"
142	                )
143	            upstream = self._parse_loss(loss)
144	            # Snapshot gradients first: if any layer raises mid-pass, roll the
145	            # partial accumulation back so the state is exactly as if backward
146	            # had never run and the caller may retry the same forward's backward
147	            # (that retry is not a second backward pass).
148	            grad_snapshot = [
149	                None if param.grad is None else param.grad.tolist()
150	                for param in self.parameters()
151	            ]
152	            try:
153	                for module in reversed(self._modules):
154	                    upstream = module.backward(upstream)
155	            except BaseException:
156	                for param, saved in zip(self.parameters(), grad_snapshot):
157	                    param.grad = None if saved is None else Tensor(saved)
158	                raise
159	            self._pending_backward = False
160	
161	    def _parse_loss(self, loss):
162	        if isinstance(loss, bool):
163	            raise ValueError("loss must be numeric, not a boolean")
164	        if isinstance(loss, (int, float, Tensor)):
165	            return loss
166	        if isinstance(loss, tuple):
167	            if len(loss) != 2:
168	                raise ValueError(
169	                    "tuple loss must be (output, upstream): exactly two elements"
170	                )
171	            output, upstream = loss
172	            if output is not self._last_output:
173	                raise ValueError(
174	                    "tuple loss must carry the Tensor returned by the "
175	                    "preceding forward() call"
176	                )
177	            if isinstance(upstream, bool) or not isinstance(
178	                upstream, (int, float, Tensor)
179	            ):
180	                raise ValueError(
181	                    "tuple loss upstream must be a number or a Tensor"
182	                )
183	            return upstream
184	        raise ValueError(
185	            "loss must be a scalar, a Tensor, or an (output, upstream) tuple"
186	        )

188	    def zero_grad(self):
189	        with self._lock:
190	            for param in self.parameters():
191	                param.grad = Tensor(_zeros(param.shape))
192	
193	    def parameters(self):
194	        with self._lock:
195	            params = []
196	            for module in self._modules:
197	                params.extend(module.parameters())
198	            return params
199	
200	    def update(self, learning_rate):
201	        """Perform one in-place step ``theta <- theta - learning_rate * grad``.
202	
203	        Every parameter is updated in fixed registration order using its
204	        accumulated gradient; parameters without a gradient slot are left
205	        untouched (their gradient is implicitly zero). Gradients are not
206	        cleared -- ``zero_grad`` remains the only way to reset them.
207	
208	        The whole step runs under the container lock, so a concurrent
209	        ``save`` or ``load`` can never observe a half-updated model.
210	        """
211	        with self._lock:
212	            if isinstance(learning_rate, bool) or not isinstance(
213	                learning_rate, (int, float)
214	            ):
215	                raise ValueError("learning rate must be a number")
216	            if learning_rate != learning_rate or learning_rate in (
217	                float("inf"),
218	                float("-inf"),
219	            ):
220	                raise ValueError("learning rate must be finite")
221	            for param in self.parameters():
222	                if param.grad is not None:
223	                    param._scaled_subtract_(param.grad, learning_rate)

225	    # -- checkpoints --------------------------------------------------------

227	    def _snapshot_document(self):
228	        params = self.parameters()
229	        return {
230	            "params": [
231	                {"s": param.shape, "v": param.tolist()} for param in params
232	            ],
233	            "grads": [
234	                {
235	                    "s": param.shape,
236	                    "v": param.grad.tolist()
237	                    if param.grad is not None
238	                    else _zeros(param.shape),
239	                }
240	                for param in params
241	            ],
242	            "hidden": None
243	            if self._last_hidden is None
244	            else [
245	                {"s": slot.shape, "v": slot.tolist()} for slot in self._last_hidden
246	            ],
247	            "layers": [
248	                {
249	                    "kind": _layer_kind(module),
250	                    "shapes": [param.shape for param in module.parameters()],
251	                }
252	                for module in self._modules
253	            ],
254	            "pending": False,
255	        }

257	    def save(self, target):
258	        """Fix the current slice-boundary training state into *target*.
259	
260	        *target* is either a filesystem path (``str``/``os.PathLike``), an
261	        existing directory used as an incremental checkpoint chain, or a
262	        ``bytearray`` used as an in-memory buffer. The snapshot records
263	        every parameter tensor, every accumulated gradient (zeros for
264	        parameters that have never received one), the current
265	        slice-boundary hidden state, the layer order with per-layer
266	        parameter shapes and the format version.
267	
268	        A boundary exists before the first segment and after every
269	        ``forward`` (the hidden state returned by that forward *is* the
270	        boundary), so saving is allowed even while the latest forward has
271	        not been back-propagated yet: the snapshot fixes the boundary
272	        state, not the in-flight activations. Saving mutates no existing
273	        state and repeated saves of the same state produce identical
274	        bytes. The whole snapshot is taken under the container lock, so a
275	        concurrent ``update`` can never leave a half-written tensor in it.
276	        """
277	        with self._lock:
278	            document = self._snapshot_document()
279	            return _checkpoint.save_bytes(document, target)
280	
281	    def load(self, source):
282	        """Restore state previously written by ``save``.
283	
284	        *source* is a filesystem path, an incremental-chain directory or a
285	        bytes-like buffer. The whole checkpoint is validated before
286	        anything is applied: the format version (version 1 is migrated
287	        item by item and the origin is recorded), every tensor shape and
288	        the layer order (count, kinds and per-layer parameter shapes) must
289	        match this container exactly. Hidden-state shapes are verified on
290	        the spot, including for a model that has never run a forward. A
291	        missing path raises ``FileNotFoundError``; any structural problem
292	        rejects the entire checkpoint with ``ValueError`` and leaves the
293	        container untouched -- nothing is partially applied or silently
294	        filled in.
295	
296	        On success returns the restored slice-boundary hidden-state list
297	        (one tensor per layer), or ``None`` when the checkpoint fixed the
298	        start-of-training state. Feed it back into the next
299	        ``forward(batch, hidden)`` to continue the sequence.
300	        """
301	        with self._lock:
302	            document, source_version = _checkpoint.load_bytes_with_source(source)
303	            self._validate_against_model(document)
304	
305	            # Build every replacement tree before touching any live state,
306	            # so a failure in the middle still leaves the model exactly as
307	            # it was (validation above already rejects malformed input, but
308	            # the rebuild is kept on the apply side as a hard guarantee).
309	            params = self.parameters()
310	            new_values = [
311	                _rebuild_tree(entry["v"], entry["s"])
312	                for entry in document["params"]
313	            ]
314	            new_grads = [
315	                Tensor(_rebuild_tree(entry["v"], entry["s"]))
316	                for entry in document["grads"]
317	            ]
318	            if document["hidden"] is None:
319	                new_hidden = None
320	                new_hidden_shapes = None
321	            else:
322	                rebuilt_slots = [
323	                    Tensor(_rebuild_tree(entry["v"], entry["s"]))
324	                    for entry in document["hidden"]
325	                ]
326	                new_hidden = rebuilt_slots
327	                new_hidden_shapes = [slot.shape for slot in rebuilt_slots]
328	
329	            for param, values in zip(params, new_values):
330	                param._set_values(values)
331	            for param, grad in zip(params, new_grads):
332	                param.grad = grad
333	            self._last_hidden = new_hidden
334	            self._hidden_shapes = new_hidden_shapes
335	            self._last_output = None
336	            self._pending_backward = False
337	            self._loaded_from_version = source_version
338	            if new_hidden is None:
339	                return None
340	            return [Tensor(slot.tolist()) for slot in new_hidden]

342	    def _validate_against_model(self, document):
343	        if not isinstance(document, dict):
344	            raise ValueError("checkpoint is not a valid state document")
345	        params = self.parameters()
346	        saved_params = document.get("params")
347	        saved_grads = document.get("grads")
348	        if (
349	            not isinstance(saved_params, list)
350	            or not isinstance(saved_grads, list)
351	            or len(saved_params) != len(params)
352	            or len(saved_grads) != len(params)
353	        ):
354	            raise ValueError(
355	                "checkpoint parameter count does not match the current model"
356	            )
357	        for index, (param, p_entry, g_entry) in enumerate(
358	            zip(params, saved_params, saved_grads)
359	        ):
360	            if not isinstance(p_entry, dict) or not isinstance(g_entry, dict):
361	                raise ValueError(f"checkpoint parameter {index} is malformed")
362	            if p_entry.get("s") != param.shape or g_entry.get("s") != param.shape:
363	                raise ValueError(
364	                    f"checkpoint parameter {index} shape does not match the "
365	                    f"current model"
366	                )
367	            # Eagerly confirm the leaves agree with the declared shapes
368	            # before any live state is touched.
369	            _rebuild_tree(p_entry["v"], p_entry["s"])
370	            _rebuild_tree(g_entry["v"], g_entry["s"])
371	
372	        saved_layers = document.get("layers")
373	        if not isinstance(saved_layers, list) or len(saved_layers) != len(
374	            self._modules
375	        ):
376	            raise ValueError(
377	                "checkpoint layer count does not match the current model"
378	            )
379	        offset = 0
380	        for index, (module, saved) in enumerate(zip(self._modules, saved_layers)):
381	            if not isinstance(saved, dict):
382	                raise ValueError(f"checkpoint layer {index} is malformed")
383	            if saved.get("kind") != _layer_kind(module):
384	                raise ValueError(
385	                    f"checkpoint layer {index} kind {saved.get('kind')!r} does "
386	                    f"not match the current model"
387	                )
388	            current_shapes = [p.shape for p in module.parameters()]
389	            if saved.get("shapes") != current_shapes:
390	                raise ValueError(
391	                    f"checkpoint layer {index} parameter shapes do not match "
392	                    f"the current model"
393	                )
394	            offset += len(current_shapes)
395	        if offset != len(params):
396	            raise ValueError("checkpoint layer order does not match parameters")
397	
398	        saved_hidden = document.get("hidden")
399	        if saved_hidden is not None:
400	            if not isinstance(saved_hidden, list) or len(saved_hidden) != len(
401	                self._modules
402	            ):
403	                raise ValueError(
404	                    "checkpoint hidden slot count does not match the current model"
405	                )
406	            checkpoint_shapes = []
407	            for index, entry in enumerate(saved_hidden):
408	                if not isinstance(entry, dict) or "s" not in entry or "v" not in entry:
409	                    raise ValueError(f"checkpoint hidden slot {index} is malformed")
410	                # Verify the slot concretely on the spot: a well-formed
411	                # positive shape whose values conform. This runs even for a
412	                # model that has never executed a forward and therefore has
413	                # no recorded hidden shapes yet; the first load pins them.
414	                rebuilt = _rebuild_tree(entry["v"], entry["s"])
415	                slot_shape = Tensor(rebuilt).shape
416	                checkpoint_shapes.append(slot_shape)
417	                if self._hidden_shapes is not None and (
418	                    slot_shape != self._hidden_shapes[index]
419	                ):
420	                    raise ValueError(
421	                        f"checkpoint hidden slot {index} shape does not match "
422	                        f"the current model"
423	                    )
424	
425	        if document.get("pending") is not False:
426	            raise ValueError("checkpoint pending flag has an unexpected value")
427	
428	    def _prepare_hidden(self, hidden):
429	        count = len(self._modules)
430	        if hidden is None:
431	            return [None] * count
432	        if not isinstance(hidden, (list, tuple)) or len(hidden) != count:
433	            raise ValueError(
434	                f"hidden must be a list of {count} tensors (one slot per layer)"
435	            )
436	        slots = list(hidden)
437	        for index, slot in enumerate(slots):
438	            if slot is None:
439	                continue
440	            if not isinstance(slot, Tensor):
441	                raise ValueError(f"hidden slot {index} must be a Tensor")
442	            expected = self._hidden_shapes[index] if self._hidden_shapes else None
443	            if expected is not None and slot.shape != expected:
444	                raise ValueError(
445	                    f"hidden slot {index} has shape {slot.shape}, expected {expected}"
446	                )
447	        return slots
448	
449	
450	def _rebuild_tree(value, shape):
451	    """Validate decoded leaves against *shape* and return a fresh nested tree."""
452	    if shape:
453	        if not isinstance(value, list) or len(value) != shape[0]:
454	            raise ValueError("checkpoint tensor values do not match their shape")
455	        return [_rebuild_tree(item, shape[1:]) for item in value]
456	    if isinstance(value, (list, bool)) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
457	        raise ValueError("checkpoint tensor values do not match their shape")

1	"""Checkpoint container: versioned binary snapshots for Sequential state.
2	
3	A full snapshot fixes, in one self-describing document:
4	
5	* every parameter tensor,
6	* every accumulated gradient (zeros when a parameter has none yet),
7	* the slice-boundary hidden state of the latest boundary,
8	* the layer order and per-layer parameter shapes,
9	* the format version.
10	
11	Two on-disk shapes share the same leaf encoding and trailer:
12	
13	* **Full snapshots** (magic ``SEQECKP1``) -- one self-contained file, the
14	  format produced for file paths and in-memory buffers.
15	* **Incremental chains** -- a directory holding one full *basis* segment
16	  (``seg-00000000.seqd``) followed by delta segments that only encode the
17	  tensors that changed.  A small ``head`` pointer names the newest
18	  committed segment, so a crash between the segment write and the pointer
19	  update always recovers the previous complete state.
20	
21	Full snapshot wire format (all integers little-endian)::
22	
23	    magic        8 bytes  b"SEQECKP1"
24	    version      uint32   format version (2; version 1 is read and migrated)
25	    header_len   uint64   length of the JSON header in bytes
26	    header       header_len bytes of UTF-8 JSON (shapes, layer order, flags)
27	    payload      one leaf per tensor element, each a 1-byte tag
28	                 ("i" | "f") followed by int64 or float64
29	    end_magic    12 bytes b"SEQECKP1END"
30	    leaf_count   uint64   number of encoded leaves
31	    payload_crc  uint32   CRC-32 of the header bytes followed by the payload
32	
33	Delta segments use magic ``SEQDELTA`` / ``SEQDELTAEND`` with the same
34	framing; their header names the basis file, the segment number, the
35	hidden-slot count (or null) and the changed tensors as ``{"i", "s"}``
36	records, where *i* is the flat tensor index (params, then grads, then
37	hidden slots).
38	
39	Float leaves are emitted as raw IEEE-754 bytes, so values (including the
40	sign of negative zero) round-trip bit for bit.  Non-finite floats and
41	integers that do not fit in int64 are refused up front, and payloads that
42	merely *contain* such bit patterns are rejected on load as well.
43	
44	Loading validates the whole document before anything is handed back:
45	truncation, corruption, a version that cannot be migrated, a missing or
46	unexpected field, or any structural problem rejects the entire checkpoint
47	with ValueError; nothing is silently filled in.
48	"""
49	
50	from __future__ import annotations
51	
52	import errno
53	import json
54	import math
55	import os
56	import re
57	import struct
58	import tempfile
59	import threading
60	import zlib
61	
62	MAGIC = b"SEQECKP1"
63	END_MAGIC = b"SEQECKP1END"
64	DELTA_MAGIC = b"SEQDELTA"
65	DELTA_END_MAGIC = b"SEQDELTAEND"
66	
67	FORMAT_VERSION = 2
68	SUPPORTED_READ_VERSIONS = (1, 2)
69	
70	_TAG_INT = ord("i")
71	_TAG_FLOAT = ord("f")
72	
73	_INT64_MIN = -(2**63)
74	_INT64_MAX = 2**63 - 1
75	
76	_TMP_PREFIX = ".seqckp.tmp-"
77	_SEG_PREFIX = "seg-"
78	_SEG_SUFFIX = ".seqd"
79	_SEG_WIDTH = 10
80	_HEAD_NAME = "head"
81	_BASIS_INDEX = 0
82	
83	_FULL_HEADER_KEYS = frozenset(("v", "params", "grads", "hidden", "layers", "pending"))
84	_DOCUMENT_KEYS = frozenset(("params", "grads", "hidden", "layers", "pending"))
85	_LAYER_KEYS = frozenset(("kind", "shapes"))
86	_DELTA_HEADER_KEYS = frozenset(("v", "b", "n", "hc", "changed", "pending"))
87	# Wire records in a delta header carry just index + shape; the leaves live
88	# in the binary payload. The in-memory build input additionally carries "v".
89	_CHANGED_KEYS = frozenset(("i", "s"))
90	_CHANGED_INPUT_KEYS = frozenset(("i", "s", "v"))
91	
92	# Same-process serialisation for writes into one chain directory.  The
93	# atomic segment-then-head commit gives the same guarantee across
94	# processes; the lock merely avoids two threads racing their temp files
95	# needlessly (and serialises snapshot diffing for one directory).
96	_chain_locks_guard = threading.Lock()
97	_chain_locks: dict[str, threading.Lock] = {}
98	
99	
100	class CheckpointError(ValueError):
101	    """A checkpoint is truncated, corrupt, or structurally invalid."""
102	
103	
104	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
105	# Shape / tree helpers
106	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
107	
108	
109	def _check_shape(shape):
110	    if not isinstance(shape, list):
111	        raise CheckpointError("tensor shape must be a list of ints")
112	    for dim in shape:
113	        if isinstance(dim, bool) or not isinstance(dim, int) or dim <= 0:
114	            raise CheckpointError("tensor shape dimensions must be positive ints")
115	
116	
117	def _exact_keys(obj, keys, what):
118	    if not isinstance(obj, dict) or set(obj) != keys:
119	        raise CheckpointError(
120	            f"{what} must be an object with exactly the fields {sorted(keys)}"
121	        )
122	
123	
124	def _shape_matches(tree, shape):
125	    node = tree
126	    for dim in shape:
127	        if not isinstance(node, list) or len(node) != dim:
128	            return False
129	        node = node[0]
130	    return not isinstance(node, list)
131	
132	
133	def _shape_size(shape):
134	    size = 1
135	    for dim in shape:
136	        size *= dim
137	    return size
138	
139	
140	def _check_leaf(value):
141	    if isinstance(value, bool):
142	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint values must be numbers, not booleans")
143	    if isinstance(value, int):
144	        if not _INT64_MIN <= value <= _INT64_MAX:
145	            raise CheckpointError(
146	                "checkpoint contains an integer too large to represent (int64)"
147	            )
148	        return _TAG_INT
149	    if isinstance(value, float):
150	        if not math.isfinite(value):
151	            raise CheckpointError("checkpoint contains a non-finite floating value")
152	        return _TAG_FLOAT
153	    raise CheckpointError(
154	        f"checkpoint values must be numbers, got {type(value).__name__}"
155	    )
156	
157	
158	def _leaf_code(value):
159	    """Ordering identity for a leaf: type, value and float sign bit."""
160	    if isinstance(value, bool):
161	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint values must be numbers, not booleans")
162	    if isinstance(value, int):
163	        if not _INT64_MIN <= value <= _INT64_MAX:
164	            raise CheckpointError(
165	                "checkpoint contains an integer too large to represent (int64)"
166	            )
167	        return (0, value)
168	    if isinstance(value, float):
169	        if not math.isfinite(value):
170	            raise CheckpointError("checkpoint contains a non-finite floating value")
171	        return (1, struct.pack("<d", value))
172	    raise CheckpointError(
173	        f"checkpoint values must be numbers, got {type(value).__name__}"
174	    )
175	
176	
177	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
178	# Freezing: snapshot document -> (JSON header, binary payload chunks)
179	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
180	
181	
182	def _freeze_tree(tree, shape, payload):
183	    if shape:
184	        if not isinstance(tree, list) or len(tree) != shape[0]:
185	            raise CheckpointError("tensor tree does not match its declared shape")
186	        for item in tree:
187	            _freeze_tree(item, shape[1:], payload)
188	    else:
189	        if isinstance(tree, list):
190	            raise CheckpointError("tensor tree does not match its declared shape")
191	        tag = _check_leaf(tree)
192	        payload.append(
193	            struct.pack("<bq", _TAG_INT, tree)
194	            if tag == _TAG_INT
195	            else struct.pack("<bd", _TAG_FLOAT, tree)
196	        )
197	
198	
199	def _freeze_entry(entry, payload):
200	    _exact_keys(entry, {"s", "v"}, "tensor entry")
201	    shape = entry["s"]
202	    _check_shape(shape)
203	    tree = entry["v"]
204	    if not _shape_matches(tree, shape):
205	        raise CheckpointError("tensor tree does not match its declared shape")
206	    _freeze_tree(tree, shape, payload)
207	    return list(shape)
208	
209	
210	def _freeze_layer(layer):
211	    _exact_keys(layer, _LAYER_KEYS, "layer descriptor")
212	    kind = layer["kind"]
213	    if not isinstance(kind, str) or not kind:
214	        raise CheckpointError("layer kind must be a non-empty string")
215	    shapes = layer["shapes"]
216	    if not isinstance(shapes, list):
217	        raise CheckpointError("layer parameter shapes must be a list")
218	    for shape in shapes:
219	        _check_shape(shape)
220	    return {"kind": kind, "shapes": [list(shape) for shape in shapes]}
221	
222	
223	def _freeze(document):
224	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
225	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint document must be an object")
226	    _exact_keys(document, _DOCUMENT_KEYS, "checkpoint document")
227	    payload = []
228	
229	    entries = document.get("params")
230	    if not isinstance(entries, list):
231	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint must record a parameter tensor list")
232	    param_shapes = [_freeze_entry(entry, payload) for entry in entries]
233	
234	    grads = document.get("grads")
235	    if not isinstance(grads, list) or len(grads) != len(entries):
236	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint must record one gradient slot per parameter")
237	    grad_shapes = [_freeze_entry(entry, payload) for entry in grads]
238	    if grad_shapes != param_shapes:
239	        raise CheckpointError("parameter and gradient shapes must match")
240	
241	    hidden = document.get("hidden")
242	    if hidden is None:
243	        hidden_shapes = None
244	    else:
245	        if not isinstance(hidden, list) or not hidden:
246	            raise CheckpointError("hidden state must be a non-empty list or null")
247	        hidden_shapes = [_freeze_entry(entry, payload) for entry in hidden]
248	
249	    layers = document.get("layers")
250	    if not isinstance(layers, list) or not layers:
251	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint must record the layer order")
252	    header_layers = [_freeze_layer(layer) for layer in layers]
253	    if sum(len(layer["shapes"]) for layer in header_layers) != len(entries):
254	        raise CheckpointError("layer parameter counts do not match the parameter list")
255	
256	    pending = document.get("pending")
257	    if not isinstance(pending, bool):
258	        raise CheckpointError("pending flag must be a boolean")
259	
260	    header = {
261	        "v": FORMAT_VERSION,
262	        "params": param_shapes,
263	        "grads": grad_shapes,
264	        "hidden": hidden_shapes,
265	        "layers": header_layers,
266	        "pending": pending,
267	    }
268	    _exact_keys(header, _FULL_HEADER_KEYS, "checkpoint header")
269	    return header, payload
270	
271	
272	def build_bytes(document):
273	    """Serialize a full snapshot document to the fixed binary representation."""
274	    header, payload = _freeze(document)
275	    return _frame(MAGIC, END_MAGIC, header, payload)
276	
277	
278	def _frame(magic, end_magic, header, payload):
279	    header_bytes = json.dumps(
280	        header, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True
281	    ).encode("utf-8")
282	
283	    body = bytearray()
284	    body += magic
285	    body += struct.pack("<I", header["v"])
286	    body += struct.pack("<Q", len(header_bytes))
287	    body += header_bytes
288	    crc = zlib.crc32(header_bytes)
289	    leaf_count = 0
290	    for chunk in payload:
291	        body += chunk
292	        crc = zlib.crc32(chunk, crc)
293	        leaf_count += 1
294	    body += end_magic
295	    body += struct.pack("<Q", leaf_count)
296	    body += struct.pack("<I", crc & 0xFFFFFFFF)
297	    return bytes(body)
298	
299	
300	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
301	# Parsing: raw bytes -> validated snapshot document
302	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
303	
304	
305	class _LeafReader:
306	    def __init__(self, payload):
307	        self._payload = payload
308	        self._pos = 0
309	
310	    def _leaf(self):
311	        tag = self._payload[self._pos]
312	        chunk = self._payload[self._pos + 1 : self._pos + 9]
313	        self._pos += 9
314	        if tag == _TAG_INT:
315	            value = struct.unpack("<q", chunk)[0]
316	            return value
317	        if tag == _TAG_FLOAT:
318	            value = struct.unpack("<d", chunk)[0]
319	            if not math.isfinite(value):
320	                raise CheckpointError(
321	                    "checkpoint payload contains a non-finite floating value"
322	                )
323	            return value
324	        raise CheckpointError(f"unknown leaf tag {tag!r} in payload")
325	
326	    def tree(self, shape):
327	        if not shape:
328	            return self._leaf()
329	        return [self.tree(shape[1:]) for _ in range(shape[0])]
330	
331	    def remaining(self):
332	        return (len(self._payload) - self._pos) // 9
333	
334	
335	def _read_frame(data, magic, end_magic, what):
336	    prefix_len = len(magic) + 4 + 8
337	    if len(data) < prefix_len:
338	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} is truncated while reading its header")
339	    if data[: len(magic)] != magic:
340	        raise CheckpointError(f"not a {what} (bad magic)")
341	    (version,) = struct.unpack("<I", data[len(magic) : len(magic) + 4])
342	    (header_len,) = struct.unpack(
343	        "<Q", data[len(magic) + 4 : len(magic) + 4 + 8]
344	    )
345	    if header_len <= 0:
346	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header length is invalid")
347	
348	    trailer_pos = data.rfind(end_magic)
349	    trailer_len = len(end_magic) + 8 + 4
350	    if trailer_pos < 0 or len(data) - trailer_pos != trailer_len:
351	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} trailer is missing or the file is torn")
352	    header_start = prefix_len
353	    payload_end = trailer_pos
354	    if header_len > payload_end - header_start:
355	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header overruns the payload area")
356	    header_bytes = data[header_start : header_start + header_len]
357	
358	    (leaf_count, stored_crc) = struct.unpack(
359	        "<QI", data[trailer_pos + len(end_magic) :]
360	    )
361	    actual_crc = zlib.crc32(data[header_start:payload_end])
362	    if actual_crc != stored_crc:
363	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} CRC mismatch: the file is corrupt or torn")
364	
365	    try:
366	        header = json.loads(header_bytes.decode("utf-8"))
367	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
368	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header is invalid: {exc}") from exc
369	    if not isinstance(header, dict):
370	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header must be a JSON object")
371	    if header.get("v") != version:
372	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} header version does not match its frame")
373	
374	    payload = data[header_start + header_len : payload_end]
375	    if len(payload) != leaf_count * 9:
376	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} payload has the wrong size")
377	    return version, header, payload, leaf_count
378	
379	
380	def _parse_shape_list(value, what, allow_empty=False):
381	    if not isinstance(value, list) or (not value and not allow_empty):
382	        raise CheckpointError(f"{what} must be a list of shapes")
383	    shapes = []
384	    for shape in value:
385	        _check_shape(shape)
386	        shapes.append(list(shape))
387	    return shapes
388	
389	
390	def _parse_full_header(header, version):
391	    _exact_keys(header, _FULL_HEADER_KEYS, "checkpoint header")
392	    if not isinstance(header["v"], int) or isinstance(header["v"], bool):
393	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint version must be an integer")
394	    if header["v"] != version:
395	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint header version does not match")
396	    params = _parse_shape_list(header["params"], "params", allow_empty=True)
397	    grads = _parse_shape_list(header["grads"], "grads", allow_empty=True)
398	    if len(params) != len(grads) or params != grads:
399	        raise CheckpointError("parameter and gradient shape lists must match")
400	    if header["hidden"] is not None:
401	        hidden = _parse_shape_list(header["hidden"], "hidden")
402	    else:
403	        hidden = None
404	    layers = header["layers"]
405	    if not isinstance(layers, list) or not layers:
406	        raise CheckpointError("layer order must be a non-empty list")
407	    layer_shapes = []
408	    for index, layer in enumerate(layers):
409	        _exact_keys(layer, _LAYER_KEYS, f"layer {index} descriptor")
410	        if not isinstance(layer["kind"], str) or not layer["kind"]:
411	            raise CheckpointError(f"layer {index} kind must be a non-empty string")
412	        shapes = _parse_shape_list(
413	            layer["shapes"], f"layer {index} shapes", allow_empty=True
414	        )
415	        layer_shapes.extend(shapes)
416	    if layer_shapes != params:
417	        raise CheckpointError(
418	            "layer order/parameter shapes do not match the parameter tensor list"
419	        )
420	    if not isinstance(header["pending"], bool):
421	        raise CheckpointError("pending flag must be a boolean")
422	    return params, hidden
423	
424	
425	def parse_bytes(raw):
426	    """Validate and decode a full snapshot (v1 or v2); return the document.
427	
428	    A version-1 file is migrated item by item into the current document
429	    shape.  Any failure while migrating rejects the whole file -- nothing
430	    is partially returned or filled in.  The document itself carries no
431	    source-version field; use :func:`load_bytes_with_source` when the
432	    originating format version is needed.
433	    """
434	    document, _source = _decode_full(raw)
435	    return document
436	
437	
438	def load_bytes_with_source(source):
439	    """Like :func:`load_bytes`, also returning the source format version."""
440	    if isinstance(source, MemoryChain):
441	        document = load_chain_memory(source)
442	        return document, FORMAT_VERSION
443	    if isinstance(source, (str, os.PathLike)):
444	        path = os.fspath(source)
445	        if os.path.isdir(path):
446	            return load_chain(path), FORMAT_VERSION
447	        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
448	            raw = fh.read()
449	        return _decode_full(raw)
450	    if isinstance(source, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
451	        return _decode_full(source)
452	    raise TypeError("load source must be a path or bytes")
453	
454	
455	def _decode_full(raw):
456	    """Return ``(document, source_version)`` for one full snapshot."""
457	    if not isinstance(raw, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
458	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint must be bytes")
459	    data = bytes(raw)
460	    version, header, payload, leaf_count = _read_frame(
461	        data, MAGIC, END_MAGIC, "checkpoint"
462	    )
463	    if version not in SUPPORTED_READ_VERSIONS:
464	        raise CheckpointError(
465	            f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; this build reads "
466	            f"versions {SUPPORTED_READ_VERSIONS}"
467	        )
468	    param_shapes, hidden_shapes = _parse_full_header(header, version)
469	
470	    total_leaves = sum(_shape_size(shape) for shape in param_shapes) * 2
471	    if hidden_shapes is not None:
472	        total_leaves += sum(_shape_size(shape) for shape in hidden_shapes)
473	    if total_leaves != leaf_count:
474	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint leaf count does not match the header")
475	
476	    reader = _LeafReader(payload)
477	    params = [{"s": shape, "v": reader.tree(shape)} for shape in param_shapes]
478	    grads = [{"s": shape, "v": reader.tree(shape)} for shape in param_shapes]
479	    hidden = (
480	        None
481	        if hidden_shapes is None
482	        else [{"s": shape, "v": reader.tree(shape)} for shape in hidden_shapes]
483	    )
484	    if reader.remaining() != 0:
485	        raise CheckpointError("checkpoint payload has trailing bytes")
486	
487	    document = {
488	        "params": params,
489	        "grads": grads,
490	        "hidden": hidden,
491	        "layers": [
492	            {"kind": layer["kind"], "shapes": [list(s) for s in layer["shapes"]]}
493	            for layer in header["layers"]
494	        ],
495	        "pending": header["pending"],
496	    }
497	    if version == 1:
498	        document = _migrate_v1_document(document)
499	    return document, version
500	
501	
502	def _migrate_v1_document(document):
503	    """Migrate a decoded version-1 document into the v2 shape, item by item.
504	
505	    The two versions share the same tensor semantics, so migration is a
506	    field-by-field re-validation rather than a guess: every tensor, shape
507	    and descriptor is copied and checked individually.  A failure on any
508	    item raises and the caller rejects the whole file.
509	    """
510	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
511	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint is not a valid document")
512	    migrated = {}
513	    try:
514	        params = document["params"]
515	        grads = document["grads"]
516	        hidden = document["hidden"]
517	        layers = document["layers"]
518	        pending = document["pending"]
519	    except KeyError as exc:
520	        raise CheckpointError(
521	            f"v1 checkpoint is missing field {exc.args[0]!r}; refusing to migrate"
522	        ) from None
523	    if not isinstance(params, list) or not isinstance(grads, list):
524	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint tensor lists are malformed")
525	    if len(params) != len(grads):
526	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint param/gradient counts disagree")
527	    m_params = []
528	    m_grads = []
529	    for index, (p_entry, g_entry) in enumerate(zip(params, grads)):
530	        m_params.append(_migrate_v1_entry(p_entry, f"parameter {index}"))
531	        m_grads.append(_migrate_v1_entry(g_entry, f"gradient {index}"))
532	        if m_params[-1]["s"] != m_grads[-1]["s"]:
533	            raise CheckpointError(
534	                f"v1 parameter {index} and its gradient disagree on shape"
535	            )
536	    migrated["params"] = m_params
537	    migrated["grads"] = m_grads
538	    if hidden is None:
539	        migrated["hidden"] = None
540	    else:
541	        if not isinstance(hidden, list) or not hidden:
542	            raise CheckpointError("v1 hidden state must be a non-empty list or null")
543	        migrated["hidden"] = [
544	            _migrate_v1_entry(entry, f"hidden slot {index}")
545	            for index, entry in enumerate(hidden)
546	        ]
547	    if not isinstance(layers, list) or not layers:
548	        raise CheckpointError("v1 checkpoint must record the layer order")
549	    m_layers = []
550	    for index, layer in enumerate(layers):
551	        _exact_keys(layer, _LAYER_KEYS, f"v1 layer {index} descriptor")
552	        kind = layer["kind"]
553	        if not isinstance(kind, str) or not kind:
554	            raise CheckpointError(f"v1 layer {index} kind must be a non-empty string")
555	        shapes = layer["shapes"]
556	        if not isinstance(shapes, list):
557	            raise CheckpointError(f"v1 layer {index} shapes must be a list")
558	        m_shapes = []
559	        for shape in shapes:
560	            _check_shape(shape)
561	            m_shapes.append(list(shape))
562	        m_layers.append({"kind": kind, "shapes": m_shapes})
563	    migrated["layers"] = m_layers
564	    if not isinstance(pending, bool):
565	        raise CheckpointError("v1 pending flag must be a boolean")
566	    migrated["pending"] = pending
567	    if sum(len(layer["shapes"]) for layer in m_layers) != len(m_params):
568	        raise CheckpointError("v1 layer parameter counts do not match the parameter list")
569	    return migrated

588	            raise CheckpointError(f"v1 {what} values do not match their declared shape")

591	    else:
592	        if isinstance(tree, list):
593	            raise CheckpointError(f"v1 {what} values do not match their declared shape")
